_runners_up.kill_reason: Fails Urgent and Valuable. The post is exploratory, not blocked: the author's own wording is "seems like a logical next step", "This all sounds amazing" and "could help us out as well", with no deadline, no money on the line and no stalled work. The only stated workaround (stopping local agents each evening and restarting them each morning) is given no hours or dollar figure. The only numbers in the post (29.3 min vs 162.7 min, 44% of agent time waiting) are quoted from an arXiv paper, not measured on their own workload, and the idle-agent claim is described as "our feeling". No current spend, no budget ceiling and no quantified loss is stated, so the cost cannot be quantified without inventing it. Real was also not met: three HN searches surfaced one adjacent problem post from a different author (Max 5x quota exhaustion), not two. I read only the first hit or two of each truncated result set, so that is a shortfall in evidence, not proof that none exist. Secondary reason, which would have killed at Stage 4: the author already names first-party options (Claude routines, Claude remote control sessions, Grok bots), and the 5 thread replies point to three more (agent-swarm.dev, opencheese.dev, scheduled agents with a shared knowledge store). The thread drew 6 points and 5 comments in 6 days, and most replies were vendors pitching.

stage_2.customer: Small software team (the author writes "we" throughout) that already delegates complex, long-running coding tasks to locally run Claude Code agents and sub-agents on engineers' own machines. They are funded by flat-rate seats (Claude Pro/Max, ChatGPT Plus/Pro) rather than API billing, and shut the agents down every evening. The person is the engineer or tech lead who owns the team's agent tooling and reads agent-systems course material (Stanford CS146S, CMU 11-768) and arXiv papers. Team size, company and revenue are not stated in the post.
stage_2.where: Hacker News (Ask HN and Show HN agent threads) and the anthropics/claude-code GitHub issue tracker are the only places confirmed by this run. No subreddits, Discords, Slack groups or newsletters were verified, so none are listed.
stage_2.pays_for: Claude Pro/Max and ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscriptions, named in the post. No other spend is stated; they explicitly have not moved to API pricing or self-hosted LLMs and are asking how the costs compare.

stage_3.urgent: None found. The post contains no deadline, no blocked work and no money at risk. The team's agents work today during office hours; overnight running is framed as a "logical next step in efficiency". The questions asked are survey questions ("Is anyone running...", "How are the results? Is it an improvement?"), not a request for a fix this week.
stage_3.valuable: Not quantifiable from the evidence. The post gives no hours per week lost to the evening stop and morning restart, no current monthly spend and no dollar figure for "a fortune". _runners_up.kill_reason: The problem cannot support a product: the person with the pain is not the person who has to adopt the fix. The author is a hobbyist self-hosting developer who wants family and friends off SMS/WhatsApp for philosophical reasons, and the post itself says those people 'don't care that much about privacy, decentralization, or extensibility' and are already served by SMS. The post names no money on the line, no deadline and no blocked work; the only cost is an unmet ideological preference and one week of hobby tinkering. A friendlier client does not fix this, because the family's switching cost and the network effect of SMS/WhatsApp/iMessage are the real blockers. The author is asking for a persuasion pitch, not a tool, and nothing in the post shows willingness to pay. No web searches were run; this kill rests only on the post's own text.
